text:
Tom: Quick sync — we need a concise, repeatable protocol for quantized fair-runs (FP8 / INT8 / 4-bit + mixed). goal: apples-to-apples perf numbers and root-cause for the regression we saw yesterday.
Priya: +1. Can we lock down exact warmup, power, tokenization, and cache priming steps? last time differences in tokenization and warmup made the numbers noisy.
Jorge: Agree. Proposal: 3 phase run per config: 1) cold start warmup 2) stabilized throughput window 3) tail-latency probe. Keep the same seed inputs across all precisions.
Nina: Concrete numbers: warmup = 2 full passes over the benchmark corpus OR 2000 tokens (whichever first), then 5 measurement iterations of 10k tokens each. record p50/p95/p99 + tokens/sec.
Tom: Also enforce power cap and host clock settings. use nvidia-smi -pm 1 && nvidia-smi -pl <target-watts>. record GPU clocks: `nvidia-smi -q -d CLOCK` before run.
Priya: KV cache priming note: for decoder-only models we should prime the KV cache with the same prefix used in production. For warmup use the first 512 tokens of each prompt, not random. That reduces first-token jitter.
Jorge: Tokenization: use the canonical tokenizer from model repo at commit SHA X (we'll pin). script: 
```
python -m bench.tokenize --model-dir /mnt/models/mymodel --commit SHA_X --inputs inputs.jsonl --output tokens.pkl
```
This ensures exact same token boundaries across runs.
Nina: Calibration pass: for INT8 and 4-bit, run a separate calibration sweep (2000 examples sampled stratified by length) and save calibration artifacts. label all runs with calib_id and attach artifact URL in results.
Tom: Kernel selection: we must force the same kernel variants where possible. if runtime kernel-chooser differs, log chosen kernel names. Add `--dump-kernel-selection=out/sel.json` to the bench harness.
Priya: perf-bot, can you add a check that fails the job if kernel choices differ across precisions unexpectedly? :pray:
perf-bot: noted. I'll emit a warning if kernel selection deviates between runs for the same model+seq config.
Jorge: Measurement caveat: FP8 sometimes shows slightly higher throughput but worse sample quality on specific prompts. capture "quality delta" using the 50 eval prompts and store ROUGE/BLEU/semantic-similarity measures. don't conflate perf wins with quality losses.
Tom: Regression from yesterday: INT8 (calibrated) was ~5% slower than FP16 baseline on A100s. initial investigation points to fusion disabled in the custom attention kernel after quantization pass. nvprof shows extra kernel launches in attention path.
Nina: logs snippet from profiling: 
```
# nvprof sample (trimmed)
Kernel: multi_head_attn_fp16_fused  time 0.42ms
Kernel: multi_head_attn_int8_unfused time 0.61ms  (2x launches)
Kernel: kv_lookup_int8 time 0.05ms
```
Looks like the int8 path isn't using the fused attn kernel.
Priya: That explains the perf regression. Action: add a test that compares kernel names and micro-latencies between int8 and fp16 for 3 seq lengths (64/256/1024). If mismatch >10% we fail the PR.
Jorge: Also check autotuner outputs — maybe the kernel selector picked a safer but slower kernel because the calibration changed memory access patterns. record workspace sizes and tile choices.
Tom: For fair comparisons: same model checkpoint, same batch sizes, same sequence lengths, and same batch composition (mix of short/long). use the bench harness flag `--fixed-batch-seed` to generate deterministic batches.
Nina: Add SLO windows: report both steady-state throughput (median of measurement iterations) and the best single iteration to catch variability. publish both.
Priya: Data retention: keep raw traces (nsys/trace) for any run that shows >3% deviation from baseline. label them with run-id and upload to /artifacts/quant-bench/<run-id>.
Tom: Next steps: 1) finalize config YAML for runs 2) instrument bench harness to dump kernel selection + calib_id + tokenization SHA 3) rerun the failing INT8 job with KV priming and compare.
Jorge: I'll own step 2. will upload a draft config in the thread when ready.
Priya: I'll re-run the INT8 vs FP16 with the new priming config and attach perf-bot results. planning window tomorrow morning.
Nina: tiny thing — include temperature and sampling settings in metadata, even for perf runs (some kernels hot-path differently for sampling vs greedy).
Tom: Great. If no blockers, we'll treat this as the canonical quantized fair-run protocol and use it in the 2-week benchmark sprint. :rocket:
Priya: Thanks everyone. I'll collect config and post a final checklist once Jorge's changes land. :thumbsup:
